sources.label: Bandsintown listing — Fish Narc at Permanent Records Roadhouse, Oct 15 2026

kind: release-week package — hand-maintained, not a generator output
known: Two singles are out: 'Much Less Me' (lead single, 2026-08-18, Super 8 video by Jolie M-A) and 'Big Dumb World' (2026-09-15, video by James Hyson).
The 11-track list is published (Stereogum, 2026-08-17) and carried in full on the scene fact-block page.
Produced with Asheville's Alex Farrar (Wednesday, MJ Lenderman, Fiddlehead); vinyl LP pre-order is open through K Records.
First press has landed: RIFF Magazine's Sept 22 'Tuesday Tracks' capsule and The Reconnoiter's weekly playlist #152 (Oct 9) both carry 'Big Dumb World'.

Fall dates after release week: Oct 29 Los Angeles (Gold Diggers, with Sepe — verified on three sources; a dedicated JamBase listing adds a 7:00 PM start and the venue address, 5632 Santa Monica Blvd), Nov 6 Kingston NY and Nov 7 Ridgewood NY (single-source, Stereogum tour list only). The JamBase listing now also shows a $15 ticket line (aggregator, not a primary listing — the price stays unrecorded on the board).
open_conflicts: JamBase's schedule for Permanent Records Roadhouse on the evening of Thu Oct 15 lists Sam Buck (9:00 PM) and does not list Fish Narc. A shared bill or a listing lag would explain it; the conflict is recorded, not resolved. The free/RSVP detail rests on the venue calendar alone. A post-Oct 15 pass should re-check JamBase and the venue calendar and either close this conflict or carry it forward stated. The readiness pass (2026-10-13) opened JamBase's own Sam Buck listing directly — Oct 15, 9:00 PM, this venue — and the venue calendar itself, which still lists the Fish Narc Listening Party at 7 PM, free, RSVP. Both listings are live at once; the conflict is sharper, not resolved. Final pre-event check (Rotation 6, 2026-10-13) opened both listings again — the venue calendar still lists the party at 7 PM and JamBase still lists Sam Buck at 9:00 PM that evening; the conflict still stands.

page_states.pre_release: Countdown chips run to Oct 15 and Oct 16; the state line reads 'announced'. This is the state the page ships in.
page_states.release_day_unconfirmed: From Oct 16 until a research pass confirms the release, the state line says the date has arrived (or passed) and the archive has not yet confirmed the LP is out. The calendar never flips this page by itself.
page_states.released: After confirmation, the state line and the release chip read 'released' with the confirmation date, the party chip reads as past, and the first-capture slot below is filled. Driven entirely by this file's release.status — the page markup does not change.

steps: Re-open JamBase's Sam Buck listing for this venue/evening (https://www.jambase.com/show/sam-buck-permanent-records-roadhouse-20261015) and the venue calendar (https://roadhouse.permanentrecordsla.com/): if the party listing has rolled off the calendar into a past-events page, cite that page; if JamBase adds Fish Narc or drops Sam Buck, record exactly that.

Only on that evidence, mark the party as held in data/v1/live-dates.json (append to its note; keep the original verified listing facts and the conflict text as history) and in this file's events entry — never mark it held on the calendar alone.
Close the open conflict in this file and on signal.html / scene/uncle-release-week.html only if the re-check actually resolves it; otherwise carry it forward stated, with the new check date.
Then run the post-release flip below on or after 2026-10-16 when a pass confirms the full LP is out (K Records / distributor / streaming listing carrying the whole record, not a single).
post_party_recheck.trigger: The first research pass after the listening party ends on 2026-10-15 (7:00 PM PDT, Permanent Records Roadhouse).

signal_watch_capture.note: No capture has been logged against the release yet — the slot is empty on purpose. The first data/v1/signal-watch.json generated_at after 2026-10-16 fills it; until then every field stays null rather than estimated.

steps: data/release-week-uncle.json — set release.status to 'released', release.confirmed_at to the confirmation date, release.confirmed_by to the confirming source; set post_release_flip.state to 'flipped'.
data/v1/scene-figures.json — set fish-narc watch.status to 'released' and refresh watch.as_of / watch.note in the same pass.
data/v1/live-dates.json — the fish-narc-uncle-release event stays 'verified'; append the confirmation to its note rather than rewriting history.

Log the first Signal capture taken after the release into post_release_flip.signal_watch_capture below (the vault watch is Aster's own — the capture is logged against this release as the scene event it coincided with, never presented as Fish Narc data).
Re-run scripts/validate.sh and the release-week test (scripts/test_release_week.js) — the test's announced-state assertions invert on the flip and must be updated in the same commit.
post_release_flip.trigger: A research pass on or after 2026-10-16 confirms 'Uncle' is out (a live K Records / distributor / streaming listing carrying the full LP, not a single).

release.note: Five independent listings carried 2026-10-16 as upcoming at the 2026-10-12 sweep (Stereogum, AltPress, Consequence, upcomingvinyl, Release Wave); a 2026-10-13 re-check found Faygoluvers still carrying October 16, 2026 as the release date. No early release, no date change. This archive records 'released' only after a research pass confirms the LP is out — never on the calendar alone. A release-week readiness pass later on 2026-10-13 opened Stereogum, upcomingvinyl, AltPress and Faygoluvers again — October 16, 2026 still stands everywhere; the venue calendar and Bandsintown were also opened again for the party and held. Final pre-event check (Rotation 6, 2026-10-13 02:29 UTC): Stereogum and upcomingvinyl were opened again — October 16 stands; still announced, not out early.

subject.archive_link: Fish Narc enters this archive through producer credits on two vault tracks ('Pavement', 2019; 'Soul Shaking', 2018) — he is a scene figure, not one of the 21 title-credited collaborators.
